findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may apply the security deposit, or such portion thereof as necessary, against any attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damages to the Hotel's premises, incidental costs, outstanding room charges, service failures, cancellation penalties, or any other sum that the Group owes to the Hotel under this Agreement or arising from the Group's occupancy and use of the Hotel's facilities. The Hotel shall have no obligation to maintain the deposit in a segregated account or to preserve any portion of the deposit for any particular purpose.
findings.headline: Deposit can offset attrition, F&B shortfall and any charge
findings.finding_text: The Hotel may apply the deposit to any sum owed, including attrition and F&B shortfalls, and need not segregate it.
findings.cd_standard: Deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.proposed_language: The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or food and beverage minimum shortfalls, and may be applied only against specific, documented damage to the Hotel's premises caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear.
findings.redline_note: Restricts use of the deposit to documented damage.
findings.compromise_range: Refunded within 30–45 days of departure.

findings.quoted_text: Any remaining balance of the security deposit shall be refunded to the Group within ninety (90) days following the last day of the Event, provided that all invoices have been paid in full, all obligations have been satisfied, and no claims for damages are then pending.
findings.headline: Refund takes 90 days and depends on other conditions
findings.finding_text: Refund comes at 90 days and only if all invoices are paid and no claims are pending, so any dispute can hold the deposit.
findings.cd_standard: Refund in full within 30 days unless itemized accounting of specific documented damage.
findings.proposed_language: Any security deposit collected under this Agreement will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the Event's conclusion unless the Hotel provides Group with an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear.
findings.redline_note: Sets a defined refund window tied to itemized damage.
findings.compromise_range: Refunded within 30–45 days of departure.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall be responsible for communicating the cutoff date to all attendees and shall indemnify the Hotel against any claims arising from Group's failure to do so.
findings.headline: Group indemnifies Hotel for attendees missing the cutoff date
findings.finding_text: This makes the group answer to the Hotel for claims tied to what individual attendees do or do not book. It is an open-ended indemnity with no cap, tied to a cutoff date that is already earlier than the standard.
findings.cd_standard: Not covered by CD's standards library. Raise it at your discretion.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no commitment to any standard, policy, or practice beyond what such applicable law expressly requires, and the Group shall not be entitled to invoke any nondiscrimination clause, covenant, or principle not grounded in enforceable legal requirement.
findings.headline: No nondiscrimination commitment beyond legal minimum
findings.finding_text: The Hotel promises only what the law requires and disclaims any broader pledge to treat attendees equally. Attendees could be treated differently where local law permits it, with no contractual recourse.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against any attendee on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, family, marital, or military status, or similar grounds, even where state or federal law would allow it. If the state or city adopts legislation that allows such discrimination or bars local nondiscrimination measures, the group should be able to terminate without liability.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel charges labor and bartender fees on Group's food and beverage functions, calculated on the basis of estimated attendance, the scope of service, and the Hotel's then-current labor rates, which fees shall be itemized separately on the Group's invoice and shall be payable as part of the total food and beverage charges due under this Agreement. Labor fees shall include compensation for all service staff, supervisory personnel, and setup and breakdown labor, and the Group shall have no right to engage outside service providers or to reduce these fees by providing its own staff.
findings.headline: Labor and bartender fees charged on all functions
findings.finding_text: Labor and bartender fees apply to every function, adding cost beyond menu pricing.
findings.cd_standard: No labor, bartender or service fees for meeting the ratios; labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.
findings.redline_note: Limits labor fees to very small functions.
findings.compromise_range: Staffing ratios up to 20% looser than the standard, e.g. one server per 30 guests at plated breakfasts.

findings.quoted_text: The parties agree that the Hotel shall provide Group with menus and pricing no later than twenty-four (24) months prior to the Event dates. Any menus and prices quoted by the Hotel within the twenty-four (24) months window may not be changed by the Hotel without Group's written consent, except as provided herein. Pricing quoted outside this window may be revised at the Hotel's discretion.
findings.headline: Menu pricing is set 24 months out and revisable
findings.finding_text: Pricing is quoted up to 24 months ahead, and pricing outside that window can be revised at will, so food costs can rise against a fixed minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Menu pricing locked at signing-date pricing or set no earlier than 12 months before the Event.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will be confirmed at the Hotel's pricing in effect on the date of this Agreement, or established not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event, and once confirmed may not be changed by the Hotel without Group's written consent.
findings.redline_note: Fixes menu pricing at a defined point so the food and beverage budget is predictable.
findings.compromise_range: Shortfall billed at 35–50% of the gap. Menu pricing locked 6–12 months before arrival.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage for all services at the Hotel only vendors appointed exclusively by the Hotel or operating as part of the Hotel's in-house service divisions, and Group shall not retain, contract with, or permit on the Hotel's premises any outside vendor, supplier, decorator, caterer, audiovisual provider, florist, musician, photographer, or other service provider without the Hotel's prior written consent. Group's use of any outside vendor in violation of this requirement shall incur a surcharge of $2,500.00 for each such engagement.
findings.headline: In-house vendors mandatory; $2,500 fee per outside vendor
findings.finding_text: Group must use Hotel vendors and pays a surcharge for each outside vendor, removing price competition and adding cost.
findings.cd_standard: Group may use the vendor of its choice at no fee or surcharge; in-house vendors not mandatory.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Hotel's in-house vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.redline_note: Allows the group to choose its own vendors without surcharge.

findings.quoted_text: Should Group engage an outside vendor in contravention of this clause, Group shall pay the stated surcharge in addition to any costs incurred by the Hotel in addressing the unauthorized service provision. Such payment shall be invoiced separately and shall be due within fifteen (15) days of invoice. The Hotel's acceptance of payment shall not constitute a waiver of this requirement for future events or services.
findings.headline: Surcharge plus Hotel costs for using outside vendors
findings.finding_text: This paragraph adds open-ended Hotel costs on top of the surcharge, enforcing the mandatory-vendor rule.
findings.cd_standard: No fee or surcharge for outside vendors.
findings.proposed_language: No surcharge, fee, or cost will be assessed against Group for engaging its own vendors.
findings.redline_note: Removes charges for using the group's own vendors.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide complimentary room nights to Group based on a ratio of one (1) complimentary room per seventy-five (75) paid room nights occupied during the Event Period. The Hotel shall calculate this ratio from its folio records and shall invoice Group accordingly. Complimentary rooms shall be allocated at standard rate and shall be subject to all applicable taxes, service charges, gratuities, resort fees, and other charges as if the rooms were paid. The value of any complimentary room night shall not offset or reduce any other charges due from Group under this Agreement.
findings.headline: Complimentary rooms at 1 per 75 and charged as if paid
findings.finding_text: The ratio is 1 per 75 against a standard of 1 per 40, and complimentary rooms still carry taxes, service charges and resort fees.
findings.cd_standard: One complimentary room per 40 occupied room nights, cumulative across the block; clear formula.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall provide one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block (total room nights divided by 40). The Hotel shall calculate this ratio from its folio records and shall credit Group's master account accordingly. Complimentary rooms shall be provided free of room rate, service charge, gratuity, resort fee, and other charges.
findings.redline_note: Sets a clear cumulative formula for complimentary rooms.
findings.compromise_range: One complimentary room per 40–50 occupied room nights.

findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio of seventy-five (75) stated above is a guideline only and does not create an entitlement in Group. The award and allocation of any complimentary rooms shall be at the sole and absolute discretion of the Hotel, and the Hotel may elect to award fewer complimentary rooms than the guideline ratio would suggest or may decline to award complimentary rooms altogether. The Hotel may withdraw or reduce complimentary room credits at any time without notice. Group waives any claim for complimentary rooms in excess of those actually awarded by the Hotel.
findings.headline: Complimentary rooms are discretionary, not an entitlement
findings.finding_text: The Hotel can award fewer or no complimentary rooms and withdraw credits at any time, which contradicts the ratio it states.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms earned on a clear formula tied to actual pickup, not at Hotel's discretion.
findings.proposed_language: The complimentary room ratio stated above creates an entitlement in Group. Complimentary rooms earned under the formula may not be reduced or withdrawn by the Hotel.
findings.redline_note: Makes the complimentary room formula a firm entitlement.
findings.compromise_range: One complimentary room per 40–50 occupied room nights.

findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the grounds upon which Group effects termination, whether for cause, convenience, or otherwise, any and all termination by Group shall be deemed and treated as a cancellation subject to the cancellation damages scale set forth in this Agreement. Group acknowledges that termination and cancellation are not distinct events but rather the same occurrence governed by a single damages regime. The cancellation scale shall apply to every termination regardless of its cause, and Group waives any argument that termination for cause stands outside the cancellation framework. The Hotel's right to cancellation damages shall not be diminished by Group's assertion that the Hotel committed a material breach.
findings.headline: Every termination treated as cancellation with damages
findings.finding_text: Even a termination for the Hotel's own breach triggers the liquidated-damages scale, so the right to terminate carries no protection.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause is separate from, and never triggers, the cancellation clause's liquidated damages.
findings.proposed_language: None of the foregoing termination rights triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause, and termination under this section is separate from cancellation by Group.
findings.redline_note: Keeps termination for cause separate from the cancellation damages scale.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide pickup reports to Group showing room occupancy, rate structure, and charges incurred under the room block only upon Group's written request and at the Hotel's convenience, and no regular or periodic reporting shall be deemed a condition of this Agreement. Group shall not have a right to receive weekly, daily, or real-time updates on room block performance, and the Hotel reserves the right to provide such information in summary form and at intervals it deems appropriate. Group's requests for pickup information shall be directed to the Hotel's Group Sales Director and shall not obligate the Hotel to prepare reports on an expedited timeline.
findings.headline: No block reviews or regular pickup reports
findings.finding_text: There are no 24/12-month block reviews and no weekly pickup reports, so Group cannot manage the block before cutoff.
findings.cd_standard: Written block reviews at 24 and 12 months with flexibility to adjust; weekly pickup reports starting 60 days before cutoff.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again twelve (12) months prior to arrival. At Group's sole discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to ten percent (10%) at each review and twenty percent (20%) cumulatively, at the group rate; the resulting block becomes Group's room block commitment for purposes of the attrition clause. Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting sixty (60) days prior to the cutoff date.
findings.redline_note: Adds scheduled block reviews and weekly pickup reporting.

findings.quoted_text: Within ninety (90) days following the conclusion of Group's event on April 16, 2027, the Hotel shall provide Group with a comprehensive post-event report detailing final room block results, attendee counts, revenue by rate category, and itemized charges for all services rendered. This post-event report shall constitute the Hotel's final accounting of Group's stay and shall be deemed accurate and binding unless Group submits written objections within thirty (30) days of receiving the report.
findings.headline: Post-event report due in 90 days and deemed binding
findings.finding_text: The report comes later than 30 days, lacks final pickup reports at 10 days and key spend categories, and late delivery has no effect on payment.
findings.cd_standard: Final pickup reports with documentation within 10 days of departure; full post-event report within 30 days; late delivery may delay master account payment.
findings.proposed_language: Within ten (10) days of departure, Hotel will provide final room pickup reports with supporting documentation. Within thirty (30) days of departure, Hotel will provide a full post-event report, including rooms actualized, a reservation pace report starting 90 days prior to cutoff, suite and double-occupancy usage, a food and beverage revenue recap by Group and affiliate functions, outlet and other spend by attendees on room and master account charges, audio-visual spend, internet bandwidth usage, and exhibitor fees and revenue; failure to provide this report within thirty (30) days may delay payment of the master account.
findings.redline_note: Shortens report deadlines and expands report content.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or verify the Hotel's room block records, reservation systems, or internal accounting related to Group's event, and Group waives any audit rights it might otherwise possess under applicable law or contract principles. Group's sole recourse regarding disputed charges or occupancy shall be to submit written notice of specific objections to the Hotel's Group Sales Director within the thirty (30) day period following receipt of the post-event report.
findings.headline: Audit rights waived entirely
findings.finding_text: Group cannot check for miscoded rooms or verify occupancy, so rooms booked outside the block may never count toward pickup.
findings.cd_standard: No-cost room block audit, joint or independent by CD or Group, crediting any miscoded room regardless of rate.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a representative of Group or by permitting a ConferenceDirect or Group representative to do so independently, and Group will keep the list confidential. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system, including rooms booked at qualified brand-associate or business rates or through Internet distribution channels, will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.

findings.quoted_text: Group may terminate this Agreement only for material breach by the Hotel that remains uncured thirty (30) days after written notice. Termination for such cause does not relieve Group of liability for damages, including lost profit, diminution in value, and consequential loss incurred by the Hotel as a result of Group's election to terminate. The Hotel shall calculate all such damages from its books and records and shall provide Group with a detailed accounting upon request. Group shall pay such damages within thirty (30) days of invoice.
findings.headline: Only uncured breach allows exit, and Group still pays damages
findings.finding_text: None of the standard termination causes exist, and even a valid termination for Hotel breach leaves Group liable for Hotel's lost profit and consequential loss.
findings.cd_standard: No-liability termination with prompt refund for force majeure, pandemic, labor dispute, ownership change, renovation, facility reduction, unavailable convention center, discriminatory legislation.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that COVID-19 or any other infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees including an expired collective bargaining agreement, picketing, strike, or lockout arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting, or a change to a new build's operational date or scope; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) the convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends not being open, available, and fully operational over the Event dates; (h) the adoption of state or local legislation that permits discrimination against attendees on any basis protected under this Agreement; or (i) material breach by the Hotel that remains uncured thirty (30) days after written notice.
findings.redline_note: Lists circumstances in which the group may terminate without liability and receive a prompt refund.

findings.location_section: 23. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, the Group acknowledges that the Hotel may be subject to bankruptcy, foreclosure, receivership, or other insolvency proceedings, and that such events shall not trigger any notice requirement, termination right, or remedy available to the Group.
findings.headline: Bankruptcy and foreclosure give Group no notice or exit
findings.finding_text: Insolvency events are expressly excluded from notice and termination rights.
findings.cd_standard: Bankruptcy or foreclosure triggers notice within 30 days and a no-liability termination right.
findings.proposed_language: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, the Hotel's bankruptcy, foreclosure, receivership, or other insolvency proceedings shall trigger the notice requirement and termination right in this section.
findings.compromise_range: Hotel notice within 30–60 days of the change. Group's termination window of at least 30 days after notice.

findings.quoted_text: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Group shall forfeit the deposit paid to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel as partial compensation for the Hotel's lost revenue and costs incurred in preparation for the event. The Hotel and Group may mutually agree to reschedule the event at a later date, in which case the Hotel shall apply the forfeited deposit as a credit toward the deposit required for the rescheduled event, provided that all other terms of the agreement shall be negotiated anew. If no reschedule occurs, the Hotel shall issue no refund of the forfeited deposit to Group.
findings.headline: Deposit forfeited when Group cancels for a storm
findings.finding_text: Cancelling because of a storm costs the deposit, so the 'without liquidated damages' right is hollow.
findings.cd_standard: Storm cancellation is without liability.
findings.proposed_language: Should either party cancel under the named storm right, Hotel shall refund all deposits and prepayments to Group promptly. The Hotel and Group may mutually agree to reschedule the event at a later date, in which case the Hotel shall apply the deposit as a credit toward the deposit required for the rescheduled event.
findings.redline_note: Refunds deposits when the storm cancellation right is used, with an option to reschedule.

findings.quoted_text: The Group shall deposit with the Hotel the sum of $25,000.00 as security for the faithful performance of all obligations under this Agreement, including but not limited to the payment of room charges, the satisfaction of all food and beverage minimums, the performance of all other financial covenants, and the absence of damage to the Hotel's property caused by the Group's guests or representatives.
findings.headline: Deposit secures all financial obligations, not just damage
findings.finding_text: The deposit is tied to room charges and F&B minimums as well as damage, which commingles it with unrelated charges.
findings.cd_standard: Reasonable deposit relative to event size, not used to offset attrition or F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: The Group shall deposit with the Hotel the sum of $25,000.00 as security against documented damage to the Hotel's property caused by the Group's guests or representatives beyond normal wear and tear.
findings.redline_note: Limits the deposit's purpose to documented property damage.
findings.compromise_range: Refunded within 30–45 days of departure.

findings.quoted_text: In the event of a labor dispute, strike, work stoppage, lockout, labor action, or other labor-related event affecting the Hotel or its operations, no cancellation window or notice period is defined herein, and the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement based upon the occurrence or threatened occurrence of any such labor-related event. The Group's rights and remedies in the event of a labor dispute shall be limited to such remedies as are explicitly stated in this Agreement.
findings.headline: No right to cancel for a strike or labor dispute
findings.finding_text: Group is held to the agreement through a strike or lockout, with no cancellation right.
findings.cd_standard: Cancel without liability if a strike, lockout, picketing or expired union contract arises within 90 days of or during the event, whether or not Hotel can perform.
findings.proposed_language: If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform. Any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded. This clause supersedes all other provisions of this Agreement.
findings.redline_note: Gives the group a no-liability cancellation right for labor disruption near the event.
findings.compromise_range: Notice of contract expiry 6–12 months ahead. Cancellation without liability for disputes within 60–90 days of the event.

findings.quoted_text: All invoiced charges to the master account shall be due in full upon presentation, and the Group waives any right to dispute or withhold payment of billed amounts after receipt of an invoice from the Hotel. Invoices rendered by the Hotel shall be deemed final and binding as to all line items, including room charges, food and beverage costs, facility rentals, service charges, and ancillary fees, unless the Group provides written notice of a discrepancy within the timeframe specified in the master account documentation.
findings.headline: Group waives any right to dispute invoices
findings.finding_text: Charges are due on presentation with no dispute window, and invoices become binding within an unspecified timeframe.
findings.cd_standard: Payable upon receipt of invoice, with 30 days to dispute in good faith before finance charges accrue.
findings.proposed_language: If Group's credit is approved, the master account is payable upon receipt of invoice. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount.
findings.redline_note: Provides a defined window to review and dispute invoice charges.
findings.compromise_range: Finance charge capped at 1–1.5% per month, after a dispute window of at least 30 days.

findings.quoted_text: Should the Group fail to remit full payment of undisputed invoiced amounts by the date due, a monthly finance charge of 1.5% shall accrue on the unpaid balance, calculated from the due date until payment is received in full by the Hotel. This finance charge shall compound monthly and shall be added to the master account statement without further notice.
findings.headline: Finance charge of 1.5% per month, compounded
findings.finding_text: The rate exceeds the 1% cap and compounds, with accrual from the due date.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge not to exceed 1% per month or legal maximum, whichever is less, on unpaid undisputed balance after 30 days.
findings.proposed_language: If payment of all undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of the final invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance.
findings.redline_note: Caps the finance charge and applies it only to undisputed balances.
findings.compromise_range: Finance charge capped at 1–1.5% per month, after a dispute window of at least 30 days.

findings.quoted_text: In any action or proceeding brought by the Hotel to enforce its rights or to recover damages for breach of this Agreement, the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.headline: Hotel may recover punitive damages from Group
findings.finding_text: Only the Hotel is given punitive damages on top of actual damages, so the group's exposure in a dispute could exceed its actual losses.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and any dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, not the hotel's keeping litigation costs and home-court advantage on the group's side with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.

findings.quoted_text: Failure to pay any shortfall by the due date shall result in late charges at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, compounded monthly, on the outstanding balance.
findings.headline: Shortfall late charge of 1.5% compounded monthly
findings.finding_text: The F&B late charge is above the cap, compounds, and applies without regard to a dispute.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge capped at 1% per month or legal maximum, on late undisputed balances only.
findings.proposed_language: If payment of any undisputed shortfall is not received by the due date, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance.
findings.redline_note: Aligns the late charge on shortfalls with the master account finance charge.
findings.compromise_range: Finance charge capped at 1–1.5% per month, after a dispute window of at least 30 days.

findings.quoted_text: All transportation to and from any alternative hotel, including airport transfers, shall be the guest's own responsibility and expense, and the Hotel shall have no obligation to arrange, provide, or reimburse for any transportation costs incurred by the guest. The guest shall make all arrangements for such transportation independently.
findings.headline: No transportation or message forwarding for walked guests
findings.finding_text: Guests must fund their own transport and nothing is promised on message and mail forwarding.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary round-trip transportation and message, mail and package forwarding at Hotel's expense.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide complimentary round-trip ground transportation between the Hotel and the alternate hotel for each day the guest is displaced, and will forward the displaced guest's telephone messages, mail, and packages.
findings.redline_note: Provides transportation and message forwarding for relocated guests.

findings.quoted_text: Upon the Group's return to the Harborview Grand Hotel following any relocation, the relocated guest shall be assigned to a standard guest room without any upgrade, suite premium, room enhancement, or additional amenity as compensation for the inconvenience of relocation. The guest shall receive no reduction in room rate, no complimentary services, and no credit toward future stays.
findings.headline: No upgrade, amenity or rebate for relocated guests
findings.finding_text: Guests returning get no upgrade or amenity and the group gets no per-night compensation.
findings.cd_standard: Upgrade and GM welcome amenity on return; per-night credit to the group for each relocated night.
findings.proposed_language: When the guest returns, Hotel will provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity from the General Manager. Hotel will credit Group's master account $200 for each night a guest is relocated, regardless of that guest's rate.
findings.redline_note: Adds an upgrade, welcome amenity and per-night credit for relocated guests.

findings.quoted_text: Each night during which a guest's guaranteed reservation was relocated to an alternative hotel shall not be credited toward the Group's room pickup, occupancy count, or commission calculation, and such nights shall be excluded entirely from all metrics used to measure the Group's performance under the terms of this Agreement.
findings.headline: Walked nights excluded from pickup and commission
findings.finding_text: A walked night counts as unoccupied for attrition and complimentary rooms, so Group could pay attrition for rooms the Hotel failed to provide.
findings.cd_standard: Walked rooms credited to pickup and commissionable; no attrition for any walked night; added compensation for 10 or more walked guests or 10% of peak-night block.
findings.proposed_language: Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable at the group rate, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages if any guest is walked on any night. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.redline_note: Credits relocated nights to pickup and protects the group from attrition on those nights.

findings.quoted_text: Any revenue generated by the Hotel from the resale or release of rooms or function space originally committed to Group shall be retained in full by the Hotel as additional revenue beyond what Group owes under the terms of this agreement, including without limitation attrition charges, cancellation damages, or any other fees or charges assessed herein. Resale proceeds shall not be credited, offset, or applied against Group's outstanding obligations to the Hotel, and the Hotel shall have no duty to track, account for, or allocate resale revenue in any manner.
findings.headline: Resale proceeds kept by Hotel on top of damages
findings.finding_text: The Hotel can be paid twice for the same room, once by Group and once by the new buyer.
findings.cd_standard: Resale revenue credited against damages; damages due 30 days after meeting dates on evidence of mitigation.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will credit revenues from the resale of released rooms and function space against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold. For purposes of this calculation, the last rooms contracted or sold by Hotel during the meeting period after receiving notice of cancellation will be credited toward Group's unused block.
findings.redline_note: Credits resale proceeds against damages and ties payment timing to evidence of mitigation.
findings.compromise_range: Cancellation damages due 30–60 days after the meeting dates.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's resale efforts, the terms at which resale accommodations are offered to other customers, the identity of parties to whom space is resold, the rate at which such space is resold, and the complete records related to all resale transactions shall not be open to Group for inspection, audit, or verification of any kind. Group shall have no right to request, receive, or review documentation concerning the Hotel's resale activities, and Group shall waive any claim that the Hotel has failed to mitigate damages through inadequate resale efforts or unfavorable resale pricing.
findings.headline: Resale records closed to Group; mitigation claims waived
findings.finding_text: Group cannot verify any mitigation and gives up the right to claim failure to mitigate.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel records on mitigation, including occupancy reports, available to Group on request.
findings.proposed_language: All Hotel records relating to mitigation, including actual occupancy reports, will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.redline_note: Gives the group access to mitigation records.
findings.compromise_range: Cancellation damages due 30–60 days after the meeting dates.

findings.quoted_text: The Group shall pay all applicable rental charges for meeting rooms and function space utilized during the Event, calculated according to the Hotel's standard pricing schedule in effect at the time of booking. Such charges shall be stated separately on the Group's master account and shall be due and payable in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth elsewhere in this Agreement. The Hotel shall provide no credit, reduction, or waiver of function space rental fees regardless of Group's use of in-house audio-visual services, catering packages, or other Hotel services.
findings.headline: Meeting room rental charged and no basics included
findings.finding_text: Group pays rental for all meeting space, and no microphone, podium, power, lighting or HVAC is promised.
findings.cd_standard: Room rental waived; agenda space complimentary; wired mic, podium, power, lighting and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Room rental charges are waived, and meeting space outlined in Group's program agenda will be provided on a complimentary basis. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power (including existing power outlets), proper lighting, and HVAC.
findings.redline_note: Waives meeting room rental and includes standard room basics.

findings.quoted_text: Any reservation request received after the cutoff date of forty-five (45) days prior to arrival shall be offered accommodations, if available, only at the Hotel's prevailing rack rate in effect at the time of booking, with no access to the negotiated group rate regardless of the reason for the late request. The Hotel shall have no obligation to hold inventory beyond the cutoff date, and rooms not reserved by that date shall be released to the Hotel's general inventory for sale at the Hotel's sole discretion.
findings.headline: Rack rate after cutoff; unassigned rooms released at will
findings.finding_text: After cutoff attendees pay rack rate, and unassigned rooms are released without consultation, raising attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: Group rate continues while Hotel sells to the public; unassigned rooms held on prepayment or released after consultation.
findings.proposed_language: After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, and will refund those advance payments after the Event for any such rooms later paid for by Group attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public.
findings.redline_note: Keeps the group rate available after cutoff and protects unassigned rooms.
findings.compromise_range: 21–30 days before arrival.

findings.quoted_text: Each individual attendee's reservation shall be held at the rate negotiated for the Group, provided that the reservation remains in the attendee's original name. A name change on any individual reservation shall be treated as a new reservation at the Hotel's prevailing rate for comparable accommodations on the relevant dates, and the attendee shall be responsible for any rate difference between the Group rate and the prevailing rate.
findings.headline: Name changes lose the group rate
findings.finding_text: A substituted attendee pays the prevailing rate, and there is no confirmation commitment.
findings.cd_standard: Name changes at the group rate up to arrival; confirmations within 4 days at no charge (2 business days inside 30 days).
findings.proposed_language: Each individual attendee's reservation shall be held at the rate negotiated for the Group. Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival.
findings.redline_note: Allows name changes at the group rate and sets confirmation timing.

findings.quoted_text: An attendee who fails to arrive on the first night of his or her reservation shall be deemed to have no-showed, and the Hotel shall cancel the whole remaining reservation for that attendee without further notice or obligation to the attendee or the Group. Such cancellation shall release all rooms reserved for that attendee for the balance of the event period and shall eliminate any further claim by that attendee or the Group to those rooms.
findings.headline: First-night no-show cancels the entire stay
findings.finding_text: A late-arriving attendee loses the whole stay, which reduces pickup and raises attrition.
findings.cd_standard: No-shows reinstated for the following night at the same rate.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise.
findings.redline_note: Reinstates the remaining nights for attendees who arrive late.

findings.quoted_text: Individual reservations may be cancelled by the attendee or by the Group, without penalty or charge, only if written notice of cancellation is received by the Hotel's group reservations department more than seventy-two hours prior to the scheduled arrival date of the attendee. Individual reservations cancelled within seventy-two hours of arrival are charged one night's room and tax, which charge shall be non-refundable and shall be the sole remedy available to the Hotel for such late cancellation.
findings.headline: 72-hour cancellation deadline; fee not credited to attrition
findings.finding_text: Penalty-free cancellation ends 72 hours before arrival rather than 6 pm on arrival day, and retained fees are not credited against attrition.
findings.cd_standard: No fee if cancelled before 6 pm on arrival day; deposits refunded with 3 working days' notice; retained cancellation money credited to attrition.
findings.proposed_language: No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.
findings.redline_note: Extends penalty-free cancellation and credits retained fees toward the group's obligations.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall be deemed the prevailing party if it recovers any material relief, whether by judgment, settlement, or otherwise.
findings.headline: Hotel deemed prevailing party on any material relief
findings.finding_text: Fee-shifting favors the Hotel because partial recovery makes it the prevailing party and entitles it to the group's payment of its fees and expert costs. The group would not bear only its own fees in a dispute.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and any dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, not the hotel's keeping litigation costs and home-court advantage on the group's side with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall not receive credit toward damages owed for any revenue the Hotel subsequently earns from reselling cancelled rooms or function space, as the Hotel's ability to generate such resale revenue is contingent on market conditions beyond the Hotel's control and shall be retained entirely by the Hotel.
findings.headline: No credit for resale of cancelled rooms
findings.finding_text: Hotel keeps resale revenue in addition to full damages, with no mitigation obligation.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel must mitigate by reselling and credit proceeds against damages.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages, not to exceed the full amount of such damages.
findings.redline_note: Requires resale efforts and credits proceeds against cancellation damages.
findings.compromise_range: Room profit up to 80% of the single net group rate. Keep the sliding scale and the hotel's duty to resell.

findings.quoted_text: Should Group elect to rebook with the Hotel at a later date following cancellation of this agreement, such rebooking shall constitute a new and separate commitment and shall earn Group no credit, offset, or other financial benefit against damages that accrued under this cancellation provision prior to the rebooking.
findings.headline: No credit for damages paid if group rebooks
findings.finding_text: Damages paid are forfeited even if the group or a ConferenceDirect client later rebooks the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: Damages paid credited back toward a rebooking within 3 years.
findings.proposed_language: Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid; if the rebooking group is not the group that paid, the credit will be refunded directly to the group that paid.
findings.redline_note: Credits cancellation damages paid toward a later rebooking.
findings.compromise_range: Room profit up to 80% of the single net group rate. Keep the sliding scale and the hotel's duty to resell.

findings.headline: No protection if Hotel closes or reduces facilities or services
findings.finding_text: The contract has no language on closures or limits of restaurants, spa, meeting space or reduced staffing, so Group has no remedy if the property is diminished before the event.
findings.cd_standard: Closure or limit over 25% of published capacity, or material staffing reduction, requires equal alternatives at Hotel's expense; no agreement in 30 days lets Group cancel without liability.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or limits, restricts, or reduces the guest-to-staff service ratio of its housekeeping, restaurant, banquet, maintenance and engineering, safety and security, or any other service in a manner a hotel industry executive would agree is material, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services, mutually agreeable and solely at Hotel's expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to Hotel, or the parties may instead modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.
findings.redline_note: Adds a remedy if facilities or services are closed or reduced before the event.
findings.compromise_range: Closures or cuts of more than 25–35% trigger the alternatives duty.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or guarantee regarding the status, scope, timing, or impact of any construction, renovation, maintenance, or capital improvement work that may be planned, in progress, or completed during the dates of the Event or at any time during the term of this Agreement. The Hotel shall not be obligated to disclose to the Group the existence of, the nature of, or any details concerning any such work, whether affecting guest rooms, public spaces, or the exterior of the Hotel property.
findings.headline: No representation or disclosure on renovation
findings.finding_text: The Hotel need not disclose planned or ongoing work affecting the group's spaces.
findings.cd_standard: Representation of no current renovation plans affecting group space, other than ordinary maintenance.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance.
findings.redline_note: Adds a representation about current renovation plans.
findings.compromise_range: Written notice within 30–60 days of plans being confirmed.

findings.quoted_text: In the event that any change, amendment, or new enactment of state or local law relating to discrimination, equal treatment, or the provision of services occurs after the date of this Agreement and before or during the Event, the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement, terminate the group block, reduce the room block commitment, or claim any modification to the terms hereof.
findings.headline: No exit if discriminatory legislation is adopted
findings.finding_text: If new law allows discrimination against attendees, the group must still perform and pay in full. This could force the group to hold the event under conditions its members find unacceptable or face cancellation damages.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against any attendee on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, family, marital, or military status, or similar grounds, even where state or federal law would allow it. If the state or city adopts legislation that allows such discrimination or bars local nondiscrimination measures, the group should be able to terminate without liability.

findings.quoted_text: In the event that any construction, renovation, maintenance, or capital improvement work interferes with, disrupts, diminishes, or otherwise affects the Group's occupancy, the use and enjoyment of the Hotel's facilities, or the quality of service or accommodations provided to the Group's guests, such work shall not constitute grounds for the Group to terminate this Agreement, to claim damages or loss of value, to demand a rate reduction or credit, or to pursue any other remedy or relief against the Hotel. The Group's obligations under this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect notwithstanding any such interference or disruption.
findings.headline: No remedy or exit if construction disrupts the event
findings.finding_text: Group must perform fully even if renovation interferes with the meeting.
findings.cd_standard: Group may terminate without liability if it determines the work will interfere with its meeting.
findings.proposed_language: If Group determines the construction or remodeling will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.
findings.redline_note: Allows the group to terminate if renovation will interfere with its meeting.
findings.compromise_range: Written notice within 30–60 days of plans being confirmed.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains the absolute right to sell rooms to the general public at any rate, including rates below the rate offered to Group. The Hotel's pricing to the public shall not be limited by, constrained by, or subordinate to the rate offered to Group, and Group waives any claim that lower public rates violate any rate parity or rate protection provision.
findings.headline: Hotel may undercut the group rate; claims waived
findings.finding_text: Public rates can fall below the group rate during the event, and there is no group-to-group parity.
findings.cd_standard: No lower rate during event dates except qualified rates; group rate no higher than any other group within 7 days either side.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (government, airline, and contracted corporate negotiated rates). Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.
findings.redline_note: Protects the group rate against lower rates sold during the event dates.
findings.compromise_range: Group rate no higher than other groups' rates within 3–7 days of the event.

findings.quoted_text: Should the Hotel identify that it has sold rooms to the general public at a rate lower than Group's negotiated rate, any rate adjustment applied to Group's block shall be effective only for future reservations made after the Hotel has identified and approved the lower rate. No retroactive adjustment to Group's rate shall apply to reservations already confirmed prior to the date on which the lower rate is identified. Group's liability for rooms reserved at the original rate shall not be reduced or eliminated by the Hotel's subsequent discovery of lower public rates.
findings.headline: Rate adjustments only prospective, not retroactive
findings.finding_text: Attendees already booked pay the higher rate even when a lower rate was available.
findings.cd_standard: Adjust rate for all prior reservations to match and make it available to all attendees.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match and make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees.
findings.redline_note: Applies any lower rate to existing and future reservations.
findings.compromise_range: Group rate no higher than other groups' rates within 3–7 days of the event.

findings.quoted_text: Any rate adjustment determined by the Hotel to apply to Group's block shall be treated as a non-commissionable rate for purposes of Group's commission or rebate structure under this Agreement. An adjusted rate shall not count toward Group's room block pickup calculations, occupancy targets, or any other metric used to measure Group's performance against block commitments. The adjusted rate shall be invoiced at the new rate, but the Hotel shall make no adjustment to complimentary rooms, attrition calculations, or other block-based benefits.
findings.headline: Adjusted-rate rooms lose commission and pickup credit
findings.finding_text: Rooms at an adjusted rate are excluded from commission and pickup, which pushes the group toward attrition for a Hotel-created rate drop.
findings.cd_standard: Commission on contracted rate; rooms remain creditable to pickup, complimentary rooms, attrition and other concessions.
findings.proposed_language: Commission will be paid on the contracted rate regardless of any rate adjustment, and such rooms remain creditable toward Group's pickup, complimentary-room credits, attrition, and any other concession based on pickup.
findings.redline_note: Keeps adjusted-rate rooms counted toward commission, pickup and related benefits.
findings.compromise_range: Group rate no higher than other groups' rates within 3–7 days of the event.

findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the Hotel is located, without regard to its conflict of law principles, and the parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Maryland for the resolution of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the event, or the performance or breach hereof.
findings.headline: Hotel's home law and exclusive Maryland courts
findings.finding_text: Disputes must be litigated in the Hotel's home state under its law, which adds travel and legal cost for the group.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and any dispute venue should be the state and city where the group is located, not the hotel's keeping litigation costs and home-court advantage on the group's side with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.

findings.headline: No commission provision for ConferenceDirect
findings.finding_text: The contract says nothing about commission, so none is secured for ConferenceDirect on room revenue or damages.
findings.cd_standard: 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure; non-cancelable, non-transferable; 10% of damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Hotel agrees that Group could not have negotiated more favorable room rates, terms, and concessions had Group negotiated directly with Hotel rather than through ConferenceDirect, and Hotel and Group agree that commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable to another party or agency. Commission on any additional rooms or amendments will be no less than ten percent (10%) or the amount in this Agreement, whichever is higher, regardless of room rate paid. Should the standard hotel or brand commission percentage increase before the Event, the higher percentage will apply; should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission, or the new brand's commission if higher. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.
findings.redline_note: Adds the commission terms for the group's meeting planner.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall determine in its sole discretion the allocation and distribution of any gratuity and service charge collected from Group. The Hotel may retain the gratuity and service charge as its own revenue or may distribute a portion or all of it to service staff at the Hotel's election. No representation is made regarding the destination of these funds, and Group waives any right to direct, approve, or inquire into the allocation thereof. The amount due from Group remains unchanged regardless of how the Hotel applies the collected funds.
findings.headline: Hotel may keep all gratuity for itself
findings.finding_text: Attendees may believe they are tipping staff while the Hotel retains the money.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity fully distributed to staff who worked the event; service charge disclosed as separate and retained by Hotel.
findings.proposed_language: The gratuity will be fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any separate service charge will be disclosed as such, is not a tip, and is retained by Hotel.

findings.quoted_text: Should Group's occupancy fall below ninety percent (90%) on any night during the event period, Group shall be liable for attrition damages at the rate of one hundred percent (100%) of the nightly room rate for each unoccupied room within the block. This liability shall be calculated by multiplying the nightly room rate by the number of occupied rooms multiplied by the applicable damage rate, and such damages shall be assessed for each night on which the threshold is not met.
findings.headline: Damages at 100% of rate for each unoccupied room
findings.finding_text: Group pays gross rate, not lost profit, on every shortfall night, starting below 90%.
findings.cd_standard: 70% of the single net group rate, only for rooms below the 70% cumulative threshold, limited to rooms the hotel failed to sell.
findings.proposed_language: For each unsold room night below the seventy percent (70%) threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate (plus tax, if required by applicable law), calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between seventy percent (70%) of the room block and actual pickup.
findings.redline_note: Bases damages on lost profit and only on rooms the Hotel could not resell.
findings.compromise_range: Trigger up to 80% of the block, still measured cumulatively. Damages up to 80% of the single net group rate.

findings.quoted_text: All audio-visual equipment, services, and technology provided by the Hotel or contracted through the Hotel's approved vendors shall be priced according to the Hotel's standard rates and pricing schedule in effect at the time of the Event. The Group shall have no entitlement to pricing quoted prior to the date of this Agreement, and any quotation for audio-visual or internet services shall be deemed valid only for the date on which it was provided. The Hotel reserves the right to adjust pricing for audio-visual equipment, technical support, bandwidth, and all related services up to the time of the Event.
findings.headline: AV and internet quotes not honored; prices adjustable
findings.finding_text: Quoted pricing is not binding, no minimum bandwidth is stated, and add-ons carry no discount.
findings.cd_standard: Honor attached AV and internet quotes; minimum 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload; discount on additions.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs.
findings.redline_note: Locks in quoted AV and internet pricing and sets a minimum bandwidth.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel reserves the right to impose additional fees, surcharges, and service charges upon Group at any time, including without limitation after the execution of this Agreement. Such fees and surcharges may include, without limitation, facility fees, energy surcharges, sustainability fees, labor surcharges, and other operational charges that the Hotel may add at its discretion. Group shall pay all such fees as added to its bills, whether or not such fees were disclosed prior to Group's signature on this Agreement.
findings.headline: Hotel may add any fee after signing
findings.finding_text: Undisclosed fees can be added at will, leaving the budget open-ended.
findings.cd_standard: All charges disclosed in writing before signature; undisclosed charges waived; later add-ons need written approval.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges that may be associated with the Event based on the meeting requirements provided by Group, including but not limited to resort fees, surcharges, shipping and delivery charges, electrical charges, telephone access charges, porterage, rigging, signage, sponsorship or conference branding and marketing, and meeting setup or rental charges. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived. Should Group require additional services or equipment after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account.
findings.redline_note: Requires disclosure of all charges before signing and approval of later additions.

findings.quoted_text: Fees and surcharges disclosed in writing to Group prior to execution of this Agreement shall appear on final invoices as described. All fees and surcharges, whether pre-disclosed or introduced after execution, shall be due and payable by Group. Group waives any claim that undisclosed charges are unenforceable or that such charges constitute a material modification of the Agreement. The Hotel's right to add fees shall not be limited by prior disclosures or the absence thereof.
findings.headline: Group waives objection to undisclosed charges
findings.finding_text: Group is barred from contesting charges it never saw before signing.
findings.cd_standard: Any charge not disclosed by signature is waived outright.
findings.proposed_language: Fees and surcharges disclosed in writing to Group prior to execution of this Agreement shall appear on final invoices as described. Any fee or surcharge not disclosed in writing prior to execution is waived.
findings.redline_note: Limits billable fees to those disclosed before signing.

findings.quoted_text: The invocation of force majeure by either party shall not relieve Group of its obligations to remit the deposit and initial payment to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel despite any termination of this agreement resulting from force majeure.
findings.headline: Hotel keeps deposits even after a force majeure termination
findings.finding_text: Even when a qualifying event ends the agreement, the Hotel retains deposits and no refund or credit is issued. The group would pay for an event it could not hold, and the 48-hour notice requirement adds a further risk of losing the right.
findings.cd_standard: Either party should be able to cancel without liability when a cause beyond its control would, in its reasonable judgment, make performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable (including for health or safety reasons), or would cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate cancellations by 20% or more of attendees. Qualifying causes should explicitly include terrorism, disease and epidemics, CDC and government travel advisories, government closures and emergency declarations, and government, corporate, and educational travel restrictions, alongside the traditional list. Group should keep this right even for conditions known at signing; if Group holds a smaller meeting instead, the hotel should waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate it offers anyone. Deposits should be refunded promptly.

findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all.
findings.headline: Hotel may refuse any assignment for any reason
findings.finding_text: The group cannot transfer the agreement, even to a successor management company running the same event, without the Hotel's unrestricted approval. The assignment restriction also covers merger and restructuring and keeps the group liable after assignment.
findings.cd_standard: The group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity (common for associations that rotate management) without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, particularly where the event itself is unchanged.

findings.quoted_text: This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises, provided that Group's indemnity shall not extend to claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
findings.headline: Group indemnifies Hotel for Hotel's own negligence
findings.finding_text: The group would cover claims caused by the Hotel's own negligence, apart from sole gross negligence or willful misconduct. This could expose the group to liability for hazards it did not create.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, including each party's reasonable attorney's fees, and should survive the end of the agreement the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence. Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not indemnify Group and makes no commitment to defend Group against any claim, and Group waives any right to claim indemnification from the Hotel under this Agreement or under applicable law, except as expressly modified by the indemnity limitations set forth herein.
findings.headline: One-way indemnity and insurance burdens fall on Group
findings.finding_text: The Hotel gives no indemnity and the group waives rights it might otherwise have, while only the group must carry $5,000,000 of insurance naming the Hotel as additional insured. The group bears all risk with no reciprocal protection.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, including each party's reasonable attorney's fees, and should survive the end of the agreement the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence. Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.

findings.quoted_text: Staffing at food and beverage functions, including the assignment of servers, bartenders, runners, and other service personnel, is at the Hotel's discretion and shall be determined by the Hotel based on the number of attendees, the complexity of the menu, the duration of the function, and the Hotel's operational requirements. The Hotel shall ensure adequate staffing to provide professional service, but the Hotel's determination of adequate staffing levels shall not be subject to challenge by the Group and shall be final.
findings.headline: Staffing is left to Hotel discretion with no guaranteed ratios
findings.finding_text: No server or bartender ratios are guaranteed and the Hotel's staffing call is final, so service quality cannot be enforced.
findings.cd_standard: Guaranteed ratios: servers 1:25 plated breakfast, 1:20 plated lunch/dinner, 1:40 and 1:30 buffets; bartenders 1:75 hosted, 1:100 cash.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees.
findings.redline_note: Sets clear minimum staffing ratios for meal and bar service.
findings.compromise_range: Staffing ratios up to 20% looser than the standard, e.g. one server per 30 guests at plated breakfasts.

findings.quoted_text: If Group's actual food and beverage consumption during the Event Period falls short of the minimum guarantee, Group shall pay the shortfall in full. The Hotel shall calculate the shortfall based on the final invoice and supporting documentation from Hotel food service records. The shortfall payment rate shall be one hundred percent (100%) of the difference between the minimum guarantee and actual consumption.
findings.headline: Full shortfall billed; affiliate spend not counted
findings.finding_text: Any F&B shortfall is billed at the full difference, and nothing counts affiliate or exhibitor spend toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Shortfall billed at a fraction (e.g. 35%) of the gap; affiliate and exhibitor F&B counts toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If Group's actual food and beverage revenue (exclusive of service charge and tax) is less than the minimum guarantee, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall. The Hotel shall calculate the shortfall based on the final invoice and supporting documentation from Hotel food service records. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.redline_note: Bills only a portion of any shortfall and counts affiliated groups' spending toward the minimum.
findings.compromise_range: Shortfall billed at 35–50% of the gap. Menu pricing locked 6–12 months before arrival.

findings.quoted_text: Should Group fail to meet its room block commitment during the Event Period, all complimentary room credits earned under this clause shall be forfeited in their entirety. Attrition shall be measured by comparing the actual room nights occupied to the room block specified in this Agreement. If actual occupancy falls below one hundred percent (100%) of the block, Group shall lose all complimentary room benefits, and the Hotel shall be relieved of any obligation to provide or credit complimentary rooms. Any forfeiture of complimentary rooms shall not reduce Group's other obligations to the Hotel.
findings.headline: All complimentary rooms forfeited below 100% of block
findings.finding_text: Group loses every complimentary room if it picks up even slightly below the full block, on top of paying attrition (itself triggered below 90% night by night), so a shortfall is penalized twice. Pickup counting and internet are also silent.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms earned regardless of block attainment; all occupied rooms, audit-credited rooms and no-show/cancellation fee nights count; free in-room internet.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive complimentary rooms calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met. All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit. Each no-show fee and each cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup and used in calculating complimentary rooms and rebates. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.redline_note: Removes the forfeiture condition and counts all occupied rooms toward complimentary credits.
findings.compromise_range: One complimentary room per 40–50 occupied room nights.

findings.location_section: 23. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership
findings.quoted_text: Upon receipt of notice of a material change in brand, management, or ownership, the Group shall have the right to terminate this Agreement by providing written notice to the Hotel within ten (10) days of receipt of such notice, and such termination shall be effective upon receipt by the Hotel. Failure to provide termination notice within the ten (10) day period shall be deemed acceptance of the change and waiver of the Group's right to terminate on this ground.
findings.headline: Only 10 days to terminate, no refund
findings.finding_text: The termination window is 10 days against 30, the right is lost silently, and no refund of deposits is promised.
findings.cd_standard: Group may terminate without liability within 30 days of notice, with prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Upon receipt of notice of a material change in brand, management, or ownership, the Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) days of the notice of termination.
findings.redline_note: Lengthens the termination window and provides a prompt refund.
findings.compromise_range: Hotel notice within 30–60 days of the change. Group's termination window of at least 30 days after notice.

findings.quoted_text: The Group acknowledges and agrees that the occurrence of any labor dispute, strike, work stoppage, lockout, job action, or labor-related disruption at the Hotel shall not relieve, excuse, or reduce the Group's obligations under this Agreement, and shall not give rise to any claim for damages, abatement of charges, rate reduction, or credit. The Group shall remain obligated to pay all room charges, food and beverage minimums, facility rental fees, and all other amounts due under this Agreement notwithstanding the occurrence or impact of any labor-related event.
findings.headline: Group stays fully liable through any labor disruption
findings.finding_text: Group must keep paying room charges, minimums and fees during a strike or lockout.
findings.cd_standard: Labor cancellation right supersedes all other provisions, with prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Where Group cancels under the labor dispute provisions of this Agreement, Group is relieved of all obligations under this Agreement, including room charges, food and beverage minimums, and facility rental fees, and all deposits and payments will be promptly refunded.
findings.redline_note: Relieves the group of payment obligations when it cancels for labor disruption.
findings.compromise_range: Notice of contract expiry 6–12 months ahead. Cancellation without liability for disputes within 60–90 days of the event.

findings.location_section: 23. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide written notice to the Group in the event of a change in the Hotel's brand affiliation, management company, ownership, or controlling interest; provided, however, that the Hotel shall provide such notice no later than ninety (90) days prior to the effective date of any such change, to the extent practicable and permitted by the Hotel's corporate counsel and applicable law.
findings.headline: Notice of change is best-efforts and qualified
findings.finding_text: Notice is only commercially reasonable efforts, 'to the extent practicable', with no firm duty and no bankruptcy or foreclosure notice.
findings.cd_standard: Mandatory written notice within 30 days of a change in brand, management or ownership, or a bankruptcy/foreclosure.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing.
findings.redline_note: Makes written notice of ownership, management or brand changes a firm obligation.
findings.compromise_range: Hotel notice within 30–60 days of the change. Group's termination window of at least 30 days after notice.

findings.quoted_text: Should the National Weather Service issue a hurricane watch or named tropical storm warning that affects the Baltimore, Maryland area during the seventy-two (72) hours preceding the event arrival date of April 12, 2027, or during the event period of April 12-16, 2027, Group shall have the right to cancel this agreement without incurring liquidated damages, provided that such cancellation notice is delivered to the Hotel in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of the issuance of such warning by the National Weather Service.
